title: Encyclopaedia Britannica - Seventh edition, Volume 13, LAB-Magnetism - EB.15
text: Tars city, the metropolis of the British empire, is situated on both banks of the Thames, if the name he taken collectively, and in that sense, though chiefly within the country of Middlesex, inclusive as part of Surveyor, and, for purposes of criminal justice (by the fact of William IV, called the Central Criminal Court Act), a portion of the counties of Esexes and Ken.
